use: a history turning point, from a teacher's notes
request: These are my lecture notes on Magna Carta. Turn the key moment into a 30 second clip for my history class.

material.name: lecture-notes.txt
material.text:
Magna Carta, June 1215, Runnymede. Rebel barons force King John to seal it.
- 63 clauses, mostly feudal dues, fees, royal forests, local grievances
- Clause 39: no free man to be seized or imprisoned except by lawful judgment of his peers or by the law of the land
- Why it matters: king bound by written law; later read as root of due process
- Annulled by the Pope within months; reissued 1216, 1217, 1225

intent: A history teacher wants the turning point for a class video.
goal: The viewer knows when it happened, what the key clause says, and why it put a king under the law.
promise: A charter forced on a king, and one sentence that outlived the rest.
arc: A date and a place, a long charter, a clause held back, then its words, ending on a king placed under the law.

events.look: the charter being sealed, with the date and place

events.text: Most of it is about feudal fees and forests. But one clause will outlive everything else.
events.job: Show the charter is mostly ordinary, and that one clause is special.

holds.does: the view moves along the charter toward one clause, still unread

events.text: No free man shall be imprisoned except by the lawful judgment of his peers or the law of the land.
events.knows: No imprisonment without lawful judgment or the law of the land.
events.look: the clause's words, with 'the law of the land' standing out

events.text: A king, in writing, was placed under the law.
events.knows: The king was under the law, in writing.
events.look: the king placed below the law
